papers.title: Mouse bio-behavioral phenotyping using a digital homecage framework for long-timescale, high-resolution, and multi-factor data collection and analytics.
papers.abstract: Long-term monitoring of behavioral and physiological processes is essential for elucidating complex brain-based phenomena and disorders that develop over extended periods, such as chronic stress, circadian disruption, and metabolic syndromes. Though digital phenotyping is well-established in humans via smart devices, comparable solutions for rodent models remain limited. To address this gap, we present the Digital Homecage (DHC) system, an open-source platform that enables uninterrupted, long-timescale recording of over 20 behavioral metrics in single-housed mice. The DHC integrates video capture, operant task modules, and wheel-running data to achieve sub-second resolution in monitoring behaviors such as actigraphy, sleep, grooming, and food choice over periods spanning weeks. Initial data validate the system's capability to reveal circadian patterns across multiple spontaneous behaviors, consistently reflecting nocturnal activity. The DHC offers unique opportunities for longitudinal analyses of chronic conditions and neuropsychiatric syndromes. Its accessibility and modular design promote community-driven innovation, establishing the DHC as a transformative tool for advancing the study of complex traits in rodent models of brain function and behavior. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-69041-0.

papers.title: Beyond sleep macrostructure: a high-definition review of acupuncture's electrophysiological signatures in modulating sleep microarchitecture (spectral power, spindles, and slow oscillations).
papers.abstract: Sleep science has shifted from coarse stage-based metrics toward a microstructural perspective that treats electroencephalographic biomarkers, spectral power, sleep spindles, and slow oscillations as candidate windows onto restorative brain function. This high-definition review evaluates whether acupuncture has been shown to modify these features. Direct evidence from natural overnight sleep is currently very limited: most available electrophysiological studies were conducted during quiet wakefulness, in resting daytime EEG recordings from clinical groups, or under propofol anesthesia. These studies demonstrate that acupuncture or related electrical acupoint stimulation can produce state-, region-, and frequency-dependent changes in EEG power and network organization, but they do not yet establish increased NREM spindle density, improved slow-oscillation-spindle coupling, enhanced slow-wave morphology, memory consolidation, or glymphatic clearance. We therefore distinguish directly observed findings from indirect mechanistic support and from hypotheses that require prospective testing. Plausible pathways include ascending somatosensory influences on thalamocortical excitability, autonomic and hypothalamic effects that may reduce hyperarousal, and peripheral or central neurochemical processes involving adenosine, GABA, serotonin, and BDNF; however, the causal sequence from needling to sleep microarchitecture remains unproven. Future progress requires preregistered, adequately powered, multi-night studies using validated spindle and slow-wave detectors, explicit control estimands, and multimodal measurements. Biomarker-guided and closed-loop acupuncture should presently be regarded as a research framework rather than an established treatment strategy.

papers.title: Experience modifies the synaptome architecture in the developing and adult mouse brain.
papers.abstract: Synaptome architecture describes the spatiotemporal distribution of highly diverse excitatory synapses throughout the brain. Whether and how this architecture is impacted by experience and sensory input is unknown. We found that environmental enrichment and monocular visual deprivation drive large-scale reconfiguration of excitatory synapse populations in more than one hundred regions of the mouse brain. Different experiences modify distinct subsets of synapse types and subtypes, with patterns aligned with protein turnover rates and connectome architecture. Similarity in experience-dependent reconfiguration during development and adulthood indicates shared mechanisms of synaptome adaptation across the lifespan. Our findings support a population-selection model in which experiences drive adaptation by selectively modifying synapse types and subtypes distributed across the brain. Experience-driven reconfiguration of synaptome architecture shares features with the response to aging, sleep deprivation, brain injury and genetic mutations, supporting a unifying principle of brain adaptation.

papers.title: Thalamic Reticular Nucleus Excitability and Cholinergic Signaling are Disrupted in a Mouse Model of Alzheimer's Disease Neuropathology.
papers.abstract: The thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) forms powerful GABAergic connections with thalamic nuclei that regulate sleep, attention, and sensory processing. TRN neurons receive dense cholinergic innervation from the basal forebrain and brainstem, dynamically shaping TRN function across brain states. We previously showed reduced TRN activity and sleep deficits in amyloid precursor protein transgenic mice (APP mice), implicating TRN dysfunction as an early contributor to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathophysiology. Here, using slice electrophysiology in mice of both sexes, we determined whether changes in intrinsic membrane properties or cholinergic synaptic transmission contribute to TRN hypoactivity in APP mice. We found that TRN neurons located in the inner core and outer shell regions undergo substantial increases in excitability after the first postnatal month. In mature animals, core neurons exhibited higher firing rates and diverse firing patterns, including persistent firing, whereas shell neurons fired at lower rates and displayed more homogeneous firing patterns without persistent activity. Firing diversity in core neurons was mediated in part by low-threshold T-type Ca²⁺ channels. Cholinergic synaptic activation, mediated predominantly by basal forebrain afferents, produced biphasic excitatory-inhibitory postsynaptic responses in both core and shell neurons, with the ratio of postsynaptic excitation and inhibition varying across postsynaptic targets. Overall, cholinergic activation suppressed TRN firing. In APP mice, core neurons showed reduced intrinsic excitability and cholinergic afferents evoked postsynaptic responses with a larger muscarinic receptor-mediated inhibitory component, leading to delayed TRN firing. Together, these findings identify both intrinsic and cholinergic synaptic mechanisms that may contribute to TRN dysfunction during early AD.Significance Statement Alzheimer's disease (AD) is typically diagnosed after cognitive symptoms emerge when treatments are less effective, highlighting the need to understand preclinical disease mechanisms. Cholinergic signaling and slow-wave sleep are disrupted before symptom onset, but the mechanisms underlying these changes remain poorly understood. Because the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) receives strong cholinergic input and mediates sleep-related rhythms, it is well positioned to contribute to early AD pathophysiology. We previously found reduced TRN activity and disrupted sleep in an AD mouse model. Here, we show that intrinsic excitability and cholinergic synaptic signaling are altered in TRN neurons during preclinical AD. These changes may contribute to thalamic dysfunction and sleep disturbances, providing a potential circuit mechanism linking early AD pathology to disease progression.

papers.title: In-ear electroencephalography: a systematic review of technology, applications, challenges, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used to monitor brain activity in both clinical and research settings. However, conventional scalp EEG systems require multiple electrodes, specialised equipment, and trained personnel, which limits their practicality for long-term monitoring in everyday environments. In-ear EEG has emerged as a promising wearable alternative that enables discreet and portable neural monitoring. This systematic review examines the current state of research on in-ear EEG technologies. Twenty-four studies met the inclusion criteria and were analysed thematically. The literature highlights rapid progress in device miniaturisation and wearable design, with reported applications including sleep monitoring, seizure detection, cognitive workload assessment, fatigue monitoring, and emotion recognition. Despite these advances, challenges remain related to signal quality, spatial coverage, and motion artefacts. Further research is required to validate in-ear EEG for broader clinical and real-world applications.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation differentially recruits amygdala subregions in male and female mice
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) acutely increases negative affect, and chronic insufficient sleep is associated with an increased risk of depression. Since the amygdala regulates both emotional processing and sleep, and SD dysregulates amygdalar function, amygdala functionality may link sleep loss to emotional outcomes. To better understand this, the specific sleep-impacted amygdalar nuclei need to be fully defined. To determine the impact of acute sleep loss on the relative activation of specific amygdalar regions, we screened for the neuronal activity marker c-Fos in wildtype mice that slept undisturbed, underwent 4-h SD, or 4-h SD with 2-h recovery sleep (RS). Application of whole-brain clearing and automated cell counting identified increased c-Fos expression within the cortical subplate of both male and female mice that was localized to amygdalar regions. As the amygdala comprises multiple distinct subnuclei, we parcellated and quantified c-Fos expression within each amygdalar subnucleus. Interestingly, we found that SD-induced differential c-Fos expression patterns between sexes. In male mice, SD increased c-Fos expression across several amygdalar subnuclei, which largely reversed with RS. By contrast, SD in females increased c-Fos expression only in the anterior basolateral amygdala and the intercalated amygdala, and both subnuclei remained activated even with RS. These findings highlight sex-specific spatial distribution of SD-activated amygdala cells, which may contribute to differences in emotional processing following sleep loss and offer potential anatomical targets for mitigating SD-related mood deficits.

papers.title: Cross-cohort validation of EEG biomarkers using a pre-registered three-criterion framework: a demonstration in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
papers.abstract: Background. Despite decades of EEG biomarker development for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), no candidate has progressed to clinical deployment, partly because cross-cohort validation is rare. We aimed to develop and demonstrate a pre-registered three-criterion screening framework to identify which candidate EEG features show the combined properties required for biomarker translation: cross-sectional discrimination, within-subject reliability, and cross-cohort effect consistency. Methods. We pre-registered a validation framework adapted from FDA-NIH BEST principles and applied it to 18 EEG features across three independent cohorts: EEGET-ALS (six ALS patients, 170 healthy controls; home recordings over 17 days), UCL/Penn State (eight ALS patients; clinic recordings over 1-2 months), and a healthy adult test-retest reference (60 participants, three sessions over one month). Features were required to meet three pre-registered criteria: (1) cross-sectional discrimination (Cohen's d > 0.5), (2) within-subject reliability (ICC(3,1) > 0.6 in both ALS cohorts independently), and (3) cross-cohort effect direction consistency. Cross-cohort permutation testing (1000 iterations) and subject-level bootstrap resampling (500 iterations) were applied to assess robustness. Results. Three features met all three pre-registered criteria: gamma power, theta power, and spectral entropy. Cross-cohort permutation testing showed that no permutation, out of 1000, produced any feature in the three-cohort reliability intersection (Monte Carlo p = 0.001). Bootstrap resampling indicated that the composition of the selected set was sensitive to sample composition (median count 1, 95% CI [0, 4]), with gamma power (67% inclusion), spectral entropy (43%), and theta power (32%) the most stable features at a relaxed reliability threshold (ICC > 0.5); at the primary pre-registered threshold (ICC > 0.6), the corresponding inclusion probabilities are lower (57%, 27%, and 19%, respectively). A principal methodological finding was that cross-cohort differences in feature reliability were large relative to the apparent disease-associated signal, most clearly demonstrated by relative beta power (ICC = 0.09 in a home-recorded cohort versus 0.93 in a clinic-recorded cohort); because recording protocol, hardware, setting, population, and preprocessing all differ jointly between cohorts in this dataset, this is evidence of cohort-associated variability that plausibly includes a protocol contribution, not a separately identified, isolated protocol effect. Conclusions. This study provides a pre-registered, multi-cohort EEG biomarker screening framework for ALS with explicit bootstrap-quantified uncertainty. Gamma power, spectral entropy, and theta power are identified as priority candidates for prospective validation. A recurring methodological observation is that protocol-related cohort differences appear to contribute more to cross-cohort variability than disease-related effects within this dataset; because protocol is confounded with cohort, equipment, and preprocessing, this pattern is descriptive rather than causal. The observation nonetheless has direct implications for the design of multi-site EEG biomarker studies in neural engineering.

papers.title: Regional cingulate metabolite-ratio differences exceed longitudinal changes across an approximately 34-h protocol: a prospective quality-controlled proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy study.
papers.abstract: Regional organization, acquisition sequence, and measurement quality can obscure the interpretation of longitudinal proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) changes. We compared anterior vs. posterior cingulate metabolite-ratio differences with changes across an approximately 34-h protocol and tested whether findings depended on sequence, quality-control rules, respiratory burden, comorbidity, or polysomnographic sleep measures. In this prospective single-center observational study, 138 university-affiliated and advertisement-recruited participants underwent baseline evening spectroscopy of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) on day 1, full-night polysomnography from day 2 into day 3, and post-PSG morning spectroscopy on day 3 using MEGA-PRESS and SVS-PRESS. Among 116 participants with complete paired timestamps, the median interval between scan starts was 34.01 h (IQR, 33.86-34.10 h). Primary metabolite-to-creatine ratios were analyzed using age-, sex-, and body mass index-adjusted generalized estimating equations. Sensitivity analyses evaluated effect magnitude, sequence dependence, spectral-quality selection, follow-up availability, exclusion of participants with apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥15 events/h, exclusion of hypertension or diabetes, and associations between metabolite change and seven polysomnographic measures. A total of 137 participants contributed to adjusted primary models. PCC showed higher NAA/Cr in both sequences and higher SVS GlxT/Cr, whereas ACC showed higher Cho/Cr in both sequences and higher MEGA Glu/Cr (all q < 0.001); PCC also showed higher MEGA GABA/Cr (q = 0.020). Cr2 denotes the vendor-fitted second creatine/phosphocreatine resonance, and GlxT denotes the sum of six vendor-fitted glutamate/glutamine components. Follow-up reductions that survived false-discovery-rate correction were confined to SVS Cr2/Cr and GlxT/Cr. Across 11 outcomes, the median absolute paired standardized effect size was 0.571 for region and 0.125 for longitudinal change; the former was 4.6 times the latter, a ratio of median standardized effect magnitudes rather than a biological fold difference. Excluding AHI ≥ 15 events/h preserved the direction of all 12 primary FDR-significant effects, with 11 remaining q < 0.05. None of 77 polysomnographic dose-response tests survived global correction. In this heterogeneous cohort, regional differences in cingulate metabolite ratios were larger and more robust than longitudinal changes. Because the approximately 34-h contrast combined elapsed time, circadian phase, an intervening monitored night, repositioning, and other uncontrolled influences, it should not be interpreted as a sleep-specific effect. The ratio-based findings should not be interpreted as regional concentration differences.

papers.title: Recovering Resting-State EEG During AM-tACS Using Dynamic Adaptive Stimulation Artifact Source Separation.
papers.abstract: Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) can modulate brain oscillations in a frequency-specific manner, but strong stimulation artifacts severely contaminate concurrent electroencephalography (EEG), limiting direct assessment of ongoing neural activity. Conventional artifact suppression methods often lack adaptability to nonstationary and frequency-dependent artifacts, which may cause incomplete artifact removal and neural signal distortion. This study aimed to develop a dynamic adaptive stimulation artifact source separation framework to improve EEG recovery during amplitude-modulated tACS (AM-tACS). We proposed a dynamic adaptive stimulation artifact source separation framework, termed DASASS, integrating recursive covariance updating, adaptive component selection, and wavelet-based multiband processing. This framework was designed to suppress time-varying and frequency-dependent stimulation artifacts while preserving the spectrotemporal and spatial characteristics of neural signals. The method was evaluated on resting-state EEG recorded during AM-tACS and compared with stimulation artifact source separation (SASS), principal component analysis (PCA), independent component analysis (ICA), and adaptive noise cancellation (ANC). Performance was assessed using normalized root mean square error, band-power deviation, and demodulated residual modulation. Microstate analysis examined whether recovered EEG preserved canonical spatial topographies and temporal dynamics. DASASS achieved the lowest NRMSE, shift-averaged NRMSE, and demodulated residual modulation among the tested methods, indicating improved waveform reconstruction and effective suppression of residual modulation artifacts, while its small negative band-power deviation suggested mild conservative attenuation rather than superior spectral preservation. Further microstate analysis showed that EEG recovered by DASASS preserved the four canonical microstate topographies, with spatial correlation coefficients ranging from 0.8643 to 0.9412 relative to the artifact-free reference EEG, while maintaining overall microstate temporal dynamics. These findings indicate that DASASS provides an effective solution for EEG recovery during AM-tACS. The proposed framework may support stimulation-state brain activity analysis and future closed-loop neuromodulation applications.

papers.title: Sleep-like slow waves during wakefulness are associated with hallucinations and poorer cognition in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Slow waves during sleep are fundamental for neural homeostasis, metabolic regulation, and waste clearance and are known to be altered in neurodegenerative diseases. Sleep-like slow waves (SLSWs) have been observed in awake, healthy individuals, where they are linked to fluctuations in vigilance and mind-wandering. Whether SLSWs are altered in Parkinson's disease (PD), and whether such alterations contribute to psychiatric or cognitive complications, remains unknown. In a cohort of 84 nondemented patients with PD and 30 healthy older adults, we found that SLSWs occurred more frequently in patients with PD. Hallucinatory traits in patients with PD were associated with higher SLSW amplitude, especially over frontocentral regions. Moreover, more prominent SLSWs were associated with poorer cognitive functions. We conclude that, whereas slow waves during sleep have positive physiological functions, exacerbated diurnal SLSWs may reflect responses related to PD neuropathology, at the cost of hallucinations and reduced cognitive function.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG spectral characteristics before and after a single auditory integration training session in children with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.abstract: Resting-state EEG characteristics may differ between autistic and non-autistic children. Conventional band power mixes periodic and broadband activity; spectral parameterization separates periodic peaks from the aperiodic background. Auditory integration training (AIT) is used as a complementary intervention, but its immediate neurophysiological and clinical effects remain uncertain. We examined baseline EEG differences and pre-post changes around one AIT session. Twenty children with ASD and 15 typically developing (TD) children aged 6-8 years participated. Resting EEG was recorded in ASD before and immediately after a 30-min Berard AIT session. Sixteen ASD participants had usable paired recordings. Relative power was measured in five bands. Periodic and aperiodic components were parameterized with FOOOF. Sensitivity analyses varied R-squared threshold, aperiodic mode, fitting settings, channel aggregation. At baseline, ASD showed higher delta and lower theta, alpha, and beta relative power than TD. After modeling peaks, aperiodic exponent and offset did not differ between groups. Among 16 paired ASD recordings, delta decreased and beta/gamma increased post-session; paired tests of exponent and offset were nonsignificant. Five of 20 baseline and seven of 18 post-session recordings had R-squared<0.90, but sensitivity analyses did not change null aperiodic findings. This uncontrolled pilot study found immediate pre-post band-power differences around one Berard AIT session but no significant FOOOF-derived aperiodic changes. Findings are hypothesis-generating and cannot distinguish AIT-specific effects from repeated measurement, arousal, expectancy, or generic auditory stimulation. Variable fit quality and small sample limit precision; controlled longitudinal studies are needed.

papers.title: Integrating wavelet signal processing and machine learning for EEG-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.
papers.abstract: BackgroundBrain diseases pose a significant global health challenge, and their diagnosis often relies on subjective clinical assessments.ObjectiveTo this end, this study proposes an integrated wavelet signal processing and machine learning framework for single-channel Electroencephalography (EEG)-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.MethodsFirst, EEG signals are decomposed into rhythm-specific sub-bands using the Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform (DWPT). Then, for each rhythm, a multi-dimensional feature matrix (MFM) is constructed by integrating Approximate Entropy (AE), Rhythm Energy Ratio (RER), C0-complexity (C0), and Zero-crossing Rate (ZCR), which comprehensively models the EEG characteristics. Six classifiers were compared under subject-level leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, and Decision Tree (DT) was selected as the representative classifier. Each channel was then evaluated independently as a complete single-channel system, and representative channels were identified from the completed results.ResultsValidated on publicly available datasets for SCHIZ (schizophrenia), UNM (Parkinson's disease), and MPHCE (depression), the method achieves impressive accuracies of 84.52% (F4), 86.54% (F4), and 93.10% (Fp1), respectively, using single-channel EEG electrode.ConclusionsSuch results demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains robust detection performance in each of the three disease-specific tasks. The framework is lightweight by design, using only a single EEG channel and a single simple machine-learning model for classification. It needs no multi-channel feature concatenation or decision-level fusion. This single-channel design suits hardware and data sources with limited resources, and may support the development of low-cost portable EEG systems.

papers.title: Sleep starts: Phenomenology and associations with sleep, psychological, and demographic characteristics.
papers.abstract: Sleep starts (SS) are transient phenomena during sleep onset. Although traditionally characterized by sudden muscle jerks, they may also involve sensory, cognitive, emotional, and autonomic experiences. Despite their high prevalence, empirical data on phenomenology and associated characteristics remain limited. This online survey examined SS phenomenology and exploratory associations with demographic, sleep-related, and psychological variables in 194 adults. Participants with self-reported sleep-related movement disorders or relevant medical conditions were excluded. Individuals reporting abrupt awakenings ≥1/week and ≥1 additional symptom formed the SS group (SS frequency ≥1, n = 96); all others the comparison group (SS frequency <1, n = 98). Because SS were operationalized using self-reported symptoms, they could not be distinguished from related sleep-onset phenomena (e.g., exploding head syndrome, hypnagogic hallucinations). Standardized questionnaires (PSQI, ISI, ESS, MZS, HADS) assessed sleep quality, insomnia severity, daytime sleepiness, dysfunctional sleep-related beliefs, and anxiety/depression symptoms. Participants described diverse experiences including motor jerks, falling sensations, dream-like experiences, somatosensory symptoms, autonomic arousal, and emotional reactions, accompanied by alarm, anxiety, and confusion. Compared with controls, the SS group reported poorer sleep quality, greater insomnia severity, stronger dysfunctional sleep-related beliefs, and higher anxiety/depressive symptoms (all p < .05). Exploratory regression analyses indicated that poorer sleep quality, stronger dysfunctional sleep-related beliefs, and higher anxiety symptoms were associated with higher SS frequency, whereas depressive symptoms were not. The final model explained 26.9% of variance (R2 = .269, adjusted R2 = .245). More frequent SS were retrospectively reported during emotional stress, whereas sleep deprivation was perceived as less influential. Although many described SS as manageable, a substantial subgroup reported distress and sleep disruption. This suggests that SS represent heterogeneous sleep-onset experiences associated with subjective sleep disturbance and cognitive-emotional arousal. Although causality cannot be inferred from cross-sectional self-report data, the results highlight potentially relevant links between SS and sleep-related cognitive-emotional processes.

papers.title: A Neuroscientific Prior-Guided Multi-View Network With Structured Channel Selection for EEG Emotion Recognition.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based emotion recognition is important for affective human-computer interaction and computer-aided mental health monitoring. Existing deep learning methods often overlook brain spatial topology or rely on complex dynamic graphs, which may introduce volume-conduction-induced spurious correlations and limit interpretability. This paper proposes SGA-MVTN, a neuroscientific prior-guided two-stage framework integrating a Multi-View Tower Network (MVTN) for prior-constrained feature modeling and a Structured Genetic Algorithm (SGA) for topology-aware channel selection. Specifically, MVTN keeps anatomically defined spatial views and frequency-band-specific spectral views separate until fusion, while SGA embeds functional grouping and hemispheric symmetry priors into evolutionary operators. Unlike spatial-spectral models operating on a fixed electrode set, the proposed framework connects view-specific representation learning with topology-aware electrode subset search. Under the leave-one-subject-out protocol, full-channel MVTN achieves 87.91% on SEED and 71.09% on SEED-IV. Under the channel-selection protocol, SGA-MVTN reduces the number of EEG channels by 54.84% while retaining 95.56% of the corresponding full-channel accuracy and achieves the highest accuracy among the evaluated reduced-channel methods. The separate towers also provide model-derived spatial and spectral importance estimates.

papers.title: Acute intermittent carotid body stimulations induce long-term facilitation of respiratory-cardiovascular coupling in rats.
papers.abstract: Hypertension, the leading modifiable risk factor for global mortality, is driven in >50% of cases by neurogenic mechanisms linked to heightened sympathetic nerve activity (SNA). A hallmark of neurogenic hypertension is the exacerbation of respiratory-modulated SNA (RespSNA) and resulting blood pressure Traube-Hering (TH) waves, which emerges during the prehypertensive period and contributes to disease development. Carotid bodies (CBs), the peripheral chemoreceptors involved in the hypoxic response, are hyperactive in hypertensive patients and animal models. Their chronic intermittent stimulation, as seen in obstructive sleep apnoea, promotes hypertension characterised by exacerbated RespSNA and TH waves. Yet, their causal role in initiating these changes remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether acute intermittent CB stimulations could directly enhance RespSNA, TH waves and blood pressure from a physiological baseline, using the in situ working heart-brainstem preparation in rats. Four brief CB stimulations with sodium cyanide, mimicking acute intermittent hypoxia, were sufficient to induce a prolonged (>20 min) increase in both inspiratory and late expiratory RespSNA bursts, TH waves and perfusion pressure, with these effects being prevented by carotid sinus denervation. These changes were accompanied by a reconfiguration of central respiratory and cardiovascular control, including elevated respiratory heart rate variability and enhanced respiratory drive targeting upper airway and abdominal muscles. Our findings demonstrate that acute intermittent CB activation triggers sustained RespSNA and elevation of TH waves, supporting its potential role in development of hypertension. Our data also suggest that CBs play a key role in initiating this respiratory-cardiovascular plasticity and that central mechanisms might contribute to its long-term maintenance. KEY POINTS: Carotid body (CB) overactivity is implicated in sympathetic excitation and development of hypertension, but its direct role in initiating respiratory-cardiovascular dysfunction remains unresolved. We tested whether brief, repeated CB stimulations could trigger lasting changes in breathing and blood pressure control from a physiological baseline. In rats, only four stimulations induced a persistent increase in respiratory-modulated sympathetic activity, elevating blood pressure fluctuations (Traube-Hering waves) and mean blood pressure. These effects, prevented by carotid sinus denervation, were linked to enhanced respiratory-cardiovascular coupling and altered upper airway and abdominal motor control. Our findings reveal that short-term CB activation can induce long-term facilitation of respiratory-cardiovascular coupling, relevant to both physiological adaptations and hypertension pathogenesis.

papers.title: Disrupted activation of dot perspective task-related EEG generators in forensic patients with borderline personality disorder.
papers.abstract: Altercentric and egocentric biases (AB, EB) refer to the impact of another agent's/own perspective on the speed with which one can report one's own/another visual perspective respectively. These biases are known to be affected by illnesses and in particular borderline personality (BPD). Coupling the dot-perspective taking task with high-density EEG recordings at the surface and in the inverse space, we analyzed the regional distribution of neural generators related to AB and EB in healthy controls (n = 24) and forensic BPD male patients (n = 14) making comparisons with previous functional MRI data obtained with the same experimental design. In both controls and BPD cases, AB was associated with early EEG activations of visual association areas. In contrast, EB was related to increased use of neural sources in salience, mentalizing networks and mirror neuron areas bilaterally. In forensic BPD patients, no statistically significant differential activation of neural generators was observed in respect to this variable. Our preliminary findings in a small sample of BPD patients show that unlike fMRI observations that pointed to an AB-related widespread increase of BOLD signal in central executive and mentalizing areas, this was not the case at the level of neural generators. Paralleling previous fMRI data, EB was related to increased need of activation of neural sources in visual association areas and later on in several networks involved in social cognition. Such activation was not observed in forensic BPD cases supporting the hypothesis of a decreased ability of these patients in mobilizing their brain resources when treating the Self-Other discrepancy. However, the limited statistical power and post-hoc group-level interaction analysis point to the need for further confirmatory analyses of these first experimental evidences. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-64677-4.

papers.title: Who gets enough sleep? - Sleep duration and classification based on sleep recommendations among the adult population in Germany.
papers.abstract: An insufficient or excessive sleep duration can be associated with various health risks. The National Sleep Foundation recommends seven to nine hours' sleep per night for 18 - 64-year-olds and seven to eight hours' sleep for adults aged 65 and older. The aim of this study is to describe the sleep duration in the adult population in Germany and to identify population groups that meet the sleep duration recommendations. Using data from the GEDA 2023 telephone survey, the mean sleep duration and the prevalence of adherence to sleep recommendations were calculated for weekdays, weekends and the whole week, stratified by gender, age group and educational group. In addition, bedtimes were grouped into categories and predicted probabilities of meeting the recommendations were estimated. On average, the adult population in Germany sleeps for 07:26 hours per night, with longer sleep duration at the weekend, particularly among 18 - 29-year-olds (07:20 hours vs. 08:23 hours). On average, women sleep longer than men (07:31 hours vs. 07:20 hours). Overall, 51.6 % meet the recommended sleep duration, more frequently at weekends than on weekdays (54.7 % vs. 46.7 %) and among those with higher level of education (62.5 %). Later bedtimes are associated with a lower likelihood of meeting the recommendations. Continuous monitoring of sleep behaviour should be established as part of national health monitoring. Additional sleep parameters, such as sleep quality and sleep disorders, should also be taken into account to identify at-risk groups and to target public health measures effectively.

The systemic inflammation response index was calculated as monocyte count × neutrophil count/lymphocyte count. Unweighted pooled linear models were retained as exploratory analyses after correcting smoking skip-pattern and special-response coding; the fully adjusted sample comprised 9051 participants. papers.title: Sleep and circadian disturbances in Alzheimer's disease: clinical assessment, treatable syndromes, and limits of biomarker inference.
papers.abstract: Sleep and circadian disturbances in Alzheimer's disease (AD) affect patients and caregivers, but clinical action depends on the syndrome, measurement, and outcome under consideration. This narrative review links sleep assessment to indication-based care while distinguishing symptomatic benefit, physiological target engagement, and disease modification. A purposive literature search was supplemented by targeted checks of PubMed-indexed and original publisher records through 4 October 2026. Selected studies are described by population, AD ascertainment, comparator, and measured endpoint rather than assigned formal evidence-certainty grades. Actigraphy characterizes behavioral rest-activity patterns; melatonin timing and temperature rhythms address endogenous circadian physiology under controlled conditions. Polysomnography and quantitative electroencephalography characterize respiratory events, sleep architecture, and oscillatory activity. These measurements inform different questions and do not independently assign AD etiology or cognitive-functional stage. Clinical priorities include confirmed obstructive sleep apnea, cognition-adapted insomnia care, irregular sleep timing, medication-related effects, parasomnias, limb symptoms, and excessive daytime sleepiness. Interpretation incorporates hypoxemia, treatment exposure, comorbidity, caregiver support, and competing diagnoses. Randomized sleep benefits remain distinct from observational cognitive associations or exploratory imaging and cerebrospinal fluid changes. Human and animal studies of arousal circuits, protein dynamics, inflammation, and fluid transport provide mechanistic context, with conflicting results interpreted according to the actual experimental endpoint. The review provides a clinically organized account of selected evidence, not a comprehensive treatment ranking. Sleep care and cognitive-etiologic assessment should proceed in parallel, with follow-up matched to patient function, safety, and the specific treatment goal.

papers.title: Comparative EEG analysis of Sutra and Tantra meditations: insights into meditative states and long-term traits.
papers.abstract: The Tibetan Buddhist tradition distinguishes between two broad categories of meditation: Sutra and Tantra, which differ in the methods and mental faculties they employ. The main neurophysiological studies of Tibetan Buddhist meditation have been conducted mostly on Sutra practices; while Tantric meditation remains less studied. This publication presents a dual comparative study, using both between-groups and within-subjects design, of the neurophysiological (EEG) correlates characterizing Sutra and Tantra meditative practices, examining both the meditative states and the meditative traits. The study was carried out within the natural environment of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries in India, maintaining the socio-cultural context. Two groups of long-term practitioners (Buddhist monks of Gelug lineage), one experienced in the Tantra tradition (T-group, n = 21) and the other in the Sutra tradition (S-group, n = 20) participated in the study. A between-group cluster permutation test revealed that the groups differed in EEG alpha power during meditation, as well as in baseline resting conditions before and after meditation. Specifically, T-group demonstrated consistently lower alpha power compared to the S-group, regardless of the conditions. Thus, the observed differences are stable characteristics of the groups. The within-subjects analysis demonstrated that the conditions (meditation, and baseline resting states before and after meditation) differed only in the T-group: during meditation, an increase in individual alpha peak frequency (iAPF) was observed in the occipital leads, followed by a decrease in iAPF after meditation. We suggest that reported between-group differences represent enduring meditative traits developed through years of training in meditative techniques in the Sutra and Tantra traditions. Nevertheless, we cannot entirely exclude the possibility that these variations may also stem from certain cohort-specific characteristics unrelated to meditation. An examination of individual power spectra revealed that the absence of significant differences in EEG spectral power between conditions can be primarily attributed to the inter-individual variability in both groups. This variability, in turn, may stem from extensive expertise of highly experienced practitioners, who over years of training, develop individualized cognitive strategies for maintaining the meditative state. Our future research will focus on a more detailed quantitative analysis of inter-individual variability during meditations and on identifying additional between-group differences among practitioners in different traditions.

papers.title: Quantitative effects of sleep deprivation on digital pupillary dynamics and visual evoked potential metrics in healthy adults.
papers.abstract: The pupillary light reflex (PLR), pupillary sleepiness test (PST), and visual evoked potentials (VEPs) are crucial for assessing the functional integrity of the visual and autonomic nervous systems. These responses integrate retinal phototransduction with midbrain reflex pathways and cortical visual processing, all of which are influenced by physiological and clinical disorders. Their temporal dynamics lay the groundwork for using pupillary reflexes and cortical potentials as biomarkers of fatigue and the effects of psychoactive substances on them. This study aimed to identify physiological biomarkers of fatigue by evaluating the PLR and VEPs. These modalities were validated against the PST, pupillary unrest index parameters, and blink-rate analysis to assess autonomic and cortical contributions to fatigue. This study examined the effects of 48-hour sleep deprivation on pupillary behavior in 18 healthy adults under controlled conditions. Analysis of PLR dynamics revealed that the dilation-phase parameters DDil1 and DDil2, corresponding to pupil diameters at 20% and 80% recovery, respectively, were sensitive to changes in autonomic activation. These complemented the established fatigue indices, including constriction velocity, relative amplitude, time of minimum diameter, and latency. Visual evoked potentials analysis demonstrated that sustained wakefulness modulated cortical responses, with a delay and amplitude reduction in the N145 component. Biomarkers from the pupillary reflex dilation phase and N145 LAT in VEP recordings serve as reliable indicators of fatigue severity, as corroborated by the PST and Stanford Sleepiness Scale assessments. papers.title: Pharmacotherapeutic strategies for the treatment of the most frequent psychiatric comorbidities in PTSD.
papers.abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is trauma- and stressor-related disorder frequently associated with somatic and psychiatric comorbidities. The most frequent psychiatric comorbidities are major depressive disorder (MDD), sleep disturbances, alcohol use disorders (AUD) and psychoses. The lack of clinical improvement is frequent in PTSD, and presence of comorbidities complicates PTSD treatment. This narrative review covered pharmacotherapy of common psychiatric comorbidities in PTSD (MDD, psychosis, sleep disturbances, especially obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and insomnia and AUD. We searched for novel data in reviews, randomized clinical trials, open labeled studies in English language through June 2026, identified using PubMed/MEDLINE/Web of Sciences/Google Scholar and clinical practice guidelines from the American Psychological Association for the Treatment of PTSD in adults (2025), and the US Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense from 2023. We discussed available evidence related to pharmacotherapy of PTSD with comorbidities. The vast majority of PTSD patients have at least one psychiatric comorbidity. Pharmacological treatment represents a challenge, given that pharmacological agents used to treat PTSD mostly do not affect symptoms of other comorbid disorders. Therefore, the choice of medications is highly individual, depending on the clinical presentation, tolerability issues, physical comorbidities, and patient preference.

papers.title: A volumetric threshold and age-dependent remodeling are associated with residual obstructive sleep apnea after adenotonsillectomy in children.
papers.abstract: Adenotonsillectomy is first-line treatment for pediatric obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), yet residual disease persists in a notable subset of children. Traditional preoperative assessments reflect patient characteristics rather than airway anatomy, while prior cone-beam CT (CBCT) studies required extra research-only scans. We evaluated whether postoperative CBCT-measured upper-airway volume distinguishes complete OSA resolution from residual disease, and assessed age-related postoperative soft-tissue remodeling. This single-center retrospective STROBE-compliant cohort enrolled 238 children aged 3-10 years with PSG-confirmed OSA who underwent coblation adenotonsillectomy, with clinically indicated pre- and 3-month postoperative CBCT. Postoperative OAHI <1 defined complete resolution, and OAHI ≥5 defined residual OSA. ROC and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. Mean OAHI decreased from 16.8 to 5.4 events/h (*p*<0.001). Complete resolution was achieved in 63.4% patients. The optimal postoperative airway volume cutoff was 10.5 cm³ (AUC=0.89). Postoperative volume <10.5 cm³, adenoid regrowth, high preoperative OAHI, younger age (3.0-3.9 years), and tongue-base hypertrophy were independent predictors of residual OSA. Postoperative upper-airway volume of 10.5 cm³ effectively stratifies residual OSA risk. Young age independently predicts persistent disease, likely due to incomplete soft tissue remodeling. This CBCT-based stratification uses clinically acquired imaging without extra radiation exposure.

papers.title: Symptom-Level Comorbidity Patterns Between Depression and Internet Gaming Disorder Among Adolescents: Evidence from Longitudinal Network Analysis with Gender Considerations.
papers.abstract: Adolescence is a period with an increased risk for the co-occurrence of depression and Internet gaming disorder (IGD), yet we still know little about how specific symptoms of these two conditions influence each other over time. In this study, we applied cross-lagged panel network analysis to two-wave data from a community sample of 538 adolescents (Mean age = 12.51 years; 53.7 percent female). Potential gender differences in the network structure were examined. In the overall sample and in both gender groups, depressive symptoms consistently predicted later gaming-related problems, whereas no reverse cross-disorder pathways were retained. In particular, suicidal ideation and psychomotor symptoms emerged as bridge symptoms linking depression and IGD, while sleep problems showed moderate outgoing expected influence in the overall symptom network. While boys and girls showed broadly similar patterns, some differences emerged in how specific symptoms were connected and which symptoms were most influential. These findings clarify the longitudinal symptom-level associations between depression and IGD in adolescents, suggesting that addressing key depressive symptoms may help reduce the risk of later IGD.

papers.abstract: The association between alcohol consumption and epilepsy is both complex and clinically significant. Acute alcohol intake suppresses central nervous system activity, while abrupt cessation of chronic heavy drinking can trigger rebound neuronal hyperexcitability, resulting in alcohol withdrawal seizures. In patients with epilepsy, heavy or binge drinking may increase seizure risk, particularly when concurrent with sleep deprivation, poor antiseizure medication adherence, dehydration, nutritional disturbances, or metabolic abnormalities. Alcohol-related seizures must be distinguished from alcohol withdrawal seizures, seizures associated with underlying epilepsy, and acute symptomatic seizures attributable to other causes, such as head trauma, cerebrovascular disease, infection, and metabolic disturbances. Therefore, clinical assessments should consider the amount and pattern of alcohol consumption, interval between the last drink and seizure onset, withdrawal symptoms, seizure characteristics, epilepsy history, medication adherence, and other potential precipitants. Benzodiazepines are the mainstay of acute management for alcohol withdrawal seizures, with treatment aiming to control withdrawal syndrome and prevent severe complications, in addition to preventing recurrent seizures. Although heavy alcohol consumption is associated with an increased risk of seizures and epilepsy, evidence regarding the effects of low-level alcohol consumption remains limited. Individualized risk assessment and counseling are essential in clinical practice.

papers.title: Drug-resistant epilepsy in non-NF1 RASopathies: a two-centre retrospective paediatric cohort and scoping review.
papers.abstract: To characterise drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) in non-NF1 RASopathies through a scoping review and a two-centre paediatric cohort. We searched PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase and Scopus from inception to September 2026 for terms covering non-NF1 RASopathies and epilepsy/seizures. Four reviewers independently screened records and extracted data in duplicate; discrepancies were resolved by consensus. Eligible records reported individuals with a non-NF1 RASopathy, seizure onset up to 17 years, and confirmed epilepsy. DRE was defined by ILAE (failure of ≥2 appropriate antiseizure medications [ASMs] at adequate dose). In parallel, we retrospectively identified paediatric patients with genetically confirmed Noonan syndrome (NS) or cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome (CFC) and DRE from two London centres over a five-year period; clinical, EEG and MRI features, ASMs and outcomes were abstracted. Of 801 records identified across three databases, 435 were screened following deduplication; 48 met inclusion criteria. Across the literature, NS showed lower epilepsy frequency and severity; DRE was uncommon and often associated with structural aetiologies. CFC displayed a severe, polymorphic phenotype with frequent status epilepticus and high DRE rates. Recent evidence also identified subclinical epileptiform activity, including continuous spike-and-wave during sleep, in CFC patients without overt seizures. Our cohort comprised six patients: two NS (variants in BRAF, PTPN11) and four CFC (all MAP2K1). Seizure types included tonic-clonic, focal seizures and infantile spasms; most required multiple ASMs. EEG abnormalities were non-specific. MRI showed heterogeneous findings, including mesial temporal sclerosis, cerebral atrophy, delayed myelination, and hippocampal dysgyria. Neurodevelopmental impairment (including autism spectrum disorder) was common. In non-NF1 RASopathies, DRE reflects combined genetic and structural contributors; in CFC, clinical-imaging correlations support a spectrum towards developmental and epileptic encephalopathy. Management should consider non-pharmacological options and carefully selected targeted approaches; mechanism-informed choices may be considered where appropriate, acknowledging that the supporting evidence remains observational.

papers.title: Institutional Variation in Electroencephalography Utilization in Neonates With Complex Congenital Heart Disease Across the United States and Its Association With Outcomes.
papers.abstract: Neonates with complex congenital heart disease are at increased risk for perioperative brain injury and seizures. Mixed-effects logistic regression with hospital as a random effect identified predictors of EEG utilization. Among 13 202 neonates, 1654 (12.5%) underwent EEG monitoring. EEG monitoring was performed in only 10.8% of neonates with dextro-transposition of the great arteries, 16% of those with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, and 13% of those with non- hypoplastic left heart syndrome single-ventricle lesions. EEG utilization increased from ~6% in 2016 to >14% in 2025, while seizure detection among EEG-monitored patients increased from 13% to ~26% (both P-trend<0.01). Utilization varied substantially across hospitals (0% to >40%), persisting after adjustment for surgical volume. EEG-monitored neonates had higher seizure detection (21.8% versus 5.2%), longer length of stay (33 versus 24 days), and higher hospitalization costs ($344 719 versus $174 865; all P<0.01). In multivariable analysis, EEG utilization was independently associated with seizures (OR ~4), dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and hypoplastic left heart syndrome, but not with cardiac arrest, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. EEG utilization in neonates with complex congenital heart disease is increasing but remains low and highly variable across US centers. The association of EEG use with higher mortality and costs may reflect confounding by indication or illness severity. Standardized protocols are needed to optimize neurologic monitoring and improve long-term outcomes.

papers.title: Epidemiology, Complications, and Management of Complications of Achondroplasia: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Achondroplasia is a rare genetic condition associated with considerable clinical burden. This study examined the clinical burden of achondroplasia, including epidemiology, condition complications and their management, and the estimated prevalence of common complications. A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted (September 2025) to identify articles published from 2011. As a result of heterogeneity across studies, meta-analyses of complication prevalence were restricted to pediatric and adolescent populations. Overall, 200 studies were included. Forty-five studies reported epidemiological data; the prevalence of achondroplasia ranged from one to 67 per 100,000 births. The most common neurological complications were cervicomedullary compression/craniocervical junction stenosis (mean 34%; n = 13) and foramen magnum narrowing (FMN; mean 26%; n = 21). The top respiratory complications were sleep disordered breathing (SDB; mean 60%; n = 13) and obstructive sleep apnea (mean 48%; n = 27). Ear, nose, and throat (ENT) complications comprised ear infections (mean 40%; n = 12) and hearing impairment (mean 40%; n = 16). Common orthopedic complications included kyphosis (mean 43%; n = 22) and bowing of legs or genu varum (mean 39%; n = 7). The top complications among pediatric populations were SDB (mean 65% [95% confidence interval (CI) 36, 85]; n = 13) and FMN (mean 56% [37, 73]; n = 20). Cervicomedullary decompression (mean 11%; n = 22) was a more frequent treatment option for neurologic complications than suboccipital decompression (mean 19%; n = 3). Typical interventions included ENT procedures (mean 40%; n = 37) and surgery for orthopedic complications (mean 28%; n = 27). Twenty-six studies reported complications from limb-lengthening surgeries (mean age of treatment 6.2-16.9 years). This SLR and meta-analysis underscore the significant clinical burden related to complications and their management in individuals with achondroplasia. Prevalence estimates varied widely by geography, reflecting differences in data sources, case ascertainment, and reporting practices. The high frequency and severity of complications underscore the need for effective treatments to reduce complication burden and improve patient quality of life.

papers.title: Reconsidering early Parkinson's disease: dopaminergic hyperactivation as a pre-degenerative functional stage.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurological condition primarily caused by the death of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc). However, recent research suggests a functional hyperactivity phase that precedes neuronal degeneration and may hold therapeutic potential. This study was conducted as a narrative review to synthesize evidence on early-phase dopaminergic hyperactivation in PD and different interventions that could potentially delay the onset of PD. We identified various toxins and genetic mutations that increase neuronal excitability, which eventually progresses to depletion of SNc neurons. This disrupts the circuitry of the basal ganglia, resulting in compensatory hyperactivity and increased dopamine release. Preclinical, neuroimaging, genetic, and clinical evidence supports that neurodegeneration in PD is preceded by a period of neuronal hyperactivation marked by increased glutamatergic transmission, calcium dysregulation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, revealing altered striatal connections and increased dopamine turnover. This hyperdopaminergic disorder manifests clinically as early non-motor symptoms like autonomic dysfunction, REM sleep behavior disorder, and hyposmia. Multimodal biomarkers that combine genetic, imaging, and electrophysiological data can detect this pre-degenerative stage, making early intervention possible. Calcium channel modulators, mitochondrial stabilizers, metabolic regulators, and anti-inflammatory medications that target the NRF2 and PPAR-γ pathways are examples of novel strategies for preserving neuronal integrity. Therefore, redefining PD as a disorder of reversible neuronal stress instead of permanent degeneration can lead to opportunities for both early and long-term neuroprotection.

papers.title: Nogo-related frontal theta-band activity after magnetic seizure therapy in treatment-resistant depression: an exploratory task-based EEG study.

However, its neurophysiological mechanisms-particularly those underlying conflict monitoring and response inhibition-remain unclear. Frontal midline theta-band activity indexes anterior cingulate-prefrontal cognitive-control activity and may reflect inefficient neural processing in depression. In this open-label, single-arm trial, 19 patients with TRD (16 female; mean age 20.89 ± 8.16 years; 10 of the 19 participants were minors) received 6-12 MST sessions using 100-Hz double-cone coil stimulation targeting bilateral F3/F4 frontal regions. Clinical assessments, including the 24-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD-24), Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale (HAMA), Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS), and 64-channel Go/Nogo task-based electroencephalography (EEG), were performed before and after treatment. EEG outcome measures included event-related potentials (N2/P3), time-frequency power (theta/beta), microstate dynamics, and theta-beta cross-frequency coupling. papers.title: Optimizing aprocitentan dosing in elderly Chinese patients with resistant hypertension: a PBPK/PD-circadian rhythm modeling study.
papers.abstract: Aprocitentan is a dual endothelin receptor antagonist for resistant hypertension (RH), but its optimal use in elderly Chinese patients remains unclear. This study aimed to develop an integrated physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK)/pharmacodynamic (PD)-circadian rhythm model to suggest precision dosing and administration-time optimization in this special population. A PBPK model was developed using published clinical pharmacokinetic data and linked to a direct-effect sigmoid maximal effect model. Circadian blood pressure (BP) variation was described by a triple-harmonic cosine function. After validation against independent pharmacokinetic (PK) and PD datasets, the model was extrapolated to elderly Chinese patients by incorporating age-related physiology, uridine 5'-diphospho-glucuronosyltransferase 1A1 activity variability, and mild hepatic impairment. Sensitivity analyses and simulations were performed to evaluate exposure, BP response, and dosing time. The model showed acceptable predictive performance. Sensitivity analyses indicated that aprocitentan exposure was mainly influenced by ionization-, binding-, and distribution-related parameters. Plasma unbound fraction and liver volume were the major determinants of cumulative and steady-state area under the curve (AUC), while lipophilicity predominantly affected early exposure, mean residence time, and terminal half-life. Compared with healthy elderly Caucasian subjects, simulated steady-state AUC increased by 20.6% in elderly Chinese patients and by 52.5% in those with mild hepatic impairment. Among the simulated regimens, 6.25 mg once daily provided the most balanced exposure profile and maintained AUC and maximum plasma concentration within the prespecified reference range in both populations. The model identified 12:00-13:00 as an alternative administration window associated with a favorable simulated 24-hour BP profile. Under the model-predicted regimen, simulated reductions in systolic BP/diastolic BP were 13.04/8.97 mmHg in elderly Chinese RH patients and 13.63/9.37 mmHg in those with mild hepatic impairment, with 24-hour BP remaining mainly within the Grade 1 hypertension range. This study established an integrated PBPK/PD-circadian rhythm model for aprocitentan in elderly Chinese patients with RH. The simulations identified 6.25 mg once daily and midday administration as candidate strategies for further clinical evaluation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective PK/PD, ambulatory BP, safety, adherence, and clinical validation before implementation in clinical practice.

papers.title: International Survey of Stereo-EEG Practices: A Comparative Analysis of Epilepsy Surgery Centers in Europe and North America.
papers.abstract: Stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) is widely used for presurgical evaluation in epilepsy, yet practice patterns vary substantially across centers, contributing to heterogeneity in the literature. We examined differences in SEEG experience, techniques, and complications across Europe and North America centers. An electronic 39-item REDCap survey was distributed to centers participating in the American Stereo-EEG Consortium and EpiCARE Consortium. The survey assessed center characteristics, electrode planning and implantation, monitoring practices, and complications. Sixty-six centers responded, including 38 from North America and 28 from Europe. North American centers more frequently used nurse-led ictal and postictal assessments (16/38 vs. 5/28; P = 0.06) and robotic image-guided implantation systems (37/38 vs. 17/28; P < 0.001), with a trend toward higher case volumes. Compared with European centers, North American programs were less likely to have over 15 years of SEEG experience (6/38 vs. 12/28; P = 0.015), fewer dedicated SEEG readers (12/38 vs. 25/28; P < 0.001), and less frequent use of SEEG-guided radiofrequency ablation (13/38 vs. 25/28; P < 0.01). Symptomatic hemorrhage was more frequently reported among North American centers in the unadjusted analysis (9/38 vs. 1/28; p = 0.035); however, the regional difference was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for center SEEG experience and annual case volume. Significant differences exist between North American and European SEEG practices. North American centers more commonly use robotic implantation and manage higher volume, whereas European centers demonstrate greater experience and more frequent use of SEEG-guided ablation. These findings support the need for standardized protocols to improve safety and outcomes.

papers.title: Integrative therapies for symptom management in dementia from a palliative perspective: narrative review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
papers.abstract: Dementia affects over 55 million people worldwide, with behavioral and psychological symptoms (BPSD) impacting over 90% of individuals. Conventional pharmacotherapies offer limited benefits with substantial side effects. Integrative care therapies (ICT) represent a complementary approach, yet the evidence supporting their use has been largely absent from the palliative care literature. This narrative review synthesizes ICT systematic reviews and meta-analyses to bridge this gap. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and the Cochrane Library were searched for systematic reviews and meta-analyses published between 2015 and June 2026 evaluating ICT for dementia symptom management. Seminal earlier works were also included when updated reviews were unavailable. Individual randomized controlled trials (RCTs), validation studies, and non-English publications were excluded, except selected sources cited for mechanistic, safety, regulatory, or pivotal-trial context. Cognitive stimulation achieved the highest evidence certainty, with high-certainty evidence for communication and social interaction and moderate-certainty evidence for cognition, quality of life (QOL), and challenging behaviors. Music therapy showed moderate-certainty evidence for depression improvement but not agitation. Light therapy and movement-based mind-body therapies (MBT) demonstrated benefit across the broadest range of domains-including cognition, BPSD, and sleep-though certainty remained low-to-very-low. Massage and aromatherapy showed consistent short-term benefits for agitation and depression. Acupuncture augmented conventional medication for improvement in cognition and activities of daily living (ADL). Dietary and herbal therapies contributed primarily to cognitive domains, with Ginkgo biloba showing the most robust BPSD evidence. Cannabinoids showed preliminary evidence for agitation and in severe disease. Across modalities, effects were often limited to the treatment period, early-stage disease showed the most robust benefits, and safety profiles were favorable. Only cognitive stimulation and music therapy achieved moderate or higher Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) ratings. Multiple ICT modalities show promising evidence for dementia symptom management that aligns with palliative care principles, though most evidence is of low-to-very-low certainty. Future research should prioritize pragmatic trials in hospice and palliative care settings using outcomes meaningful to this context, including comfort, caregiver experience, and healthcare utilization.

papers.title: [Combined use of endocrine therapy with Shenqi pills and Xihuang capsules in patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer: A retrospective real-world cohort study].
papers.abstract: Objective To evaluate the impact of combination of Shenqi pills and Xihuang capsules on the survival outcome and quality of life of patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) on the basis of standard endocrine therapy. Methods This retrospective real-world cohort study enrolled 41 patients diagnosed with CRPC between April 2021 and December 2024, including 21 patients in the control group (standard endocrine therapy) and 20 patients in the treatment group (standard endocrine therapy combined with Shenqi pills and Xihuang capsules). The primary outcome measures were overall survival (OS) and radiological progression-free survival (rPFS). Secondary outcomes included quality of life (FACT-P Version 4 scale), TCM syndrome scores (Shenyang Xu, Xue Yu), and sleep quality (ISI scale). The Kaplan-Meier method, Cox proportional hazards model and linear mixed model were used for analysis, and the inverse probability weighting method (IPTW) was used for sensitivity analysis. Results By the end of the follow-up, a total of 23 deaths had occurred, accounting for 56.1% of the total cohort. The median overall survival (OS) was 22.0 months in the control group and 34.0 months in the treatment group, representing a 12.0-month extension in the treatment group; however, the between-group difference did not reach statistical significance (log-rank χ2=2.798,P=0.094). IPTW-weighted analysis showed a trend toward reduced mortality risk in the treatment group (HR=0.540,95%CI: 0.231-1.261, P=0.155). In the subgroup of patients with Gleason score ≥9, OS was superior in the treatment group compared with the control group (P=0.039); however, the treatment effect did not reach statistical significance in the multivariate Cox regression analysis (HR=0.299, 95%CI: 0.061-1.478, P=0.139). There was no statistically significant difference in radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) between the two groups (log-rank χ2=0.143, P=0.705). Regarding quality of life, FACT-P Version 4 scores increased from 73.50±11.68 at baseline to 81.50±8.45 at 12 months in the treatment group, and from 73.38±9.63 to 77.81±10.60 in the control group. The time × group interaction effect was statistically significant (P<0.05), whereas between-group differences at individual time points did not reach statistical significance after Bonferroni correction (P>0.05). The Shenyang Xu score decreased from (17.10±6.15) to (7.15±3.30) in the treatment group, and from (19.95±2.82) to (17.62±4.63) in the control group. The Xue Yu score decreased from (31.45±13.71) to (13.95±6.00) in the treatment group, and from (37.14±7.49) to (35.00±9.86) in the control group. The time × group interaction effects for both scores were statistically significant (all P<0.01). Regarding sleep quality, the ISI score decreased from (12.60±5.92) to (5.85±2.58) in the treatment group, whereas it changed from (12.29±3.39) to (12.43±4.33) in the control group. The time×group interaction effects for the Shenyang Xu, Xue Yu, and ISI scores were all statistically significant (all P<0.01). Conclusion On the basis of standard endocrine therapy, the combination of Shenqi pills and Xihuang capsules was associated with an OS benefit in the CRPC subgroup with Gleason score ≥9. This combination regimen significantly improved Shenyang Xu and Xue Yu syndromes and sleep quality in patients with CRPC, while producing a more sustained trend toward improvement in quality of life.

papers.title: Prevalence and factors associated with sleep deprivation in nursing technicians working in shifts.
papers.abstract: to estimate the prevalence of sleep deprivation among nursing technicians working in hospital shifts and identify the associated factors. a cross-sectional study was conducted at a municipal university hospital in Goiás, Brazil, between March and May 2022, with 198 participants. papers.title: Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome in an elderly female: A video-based case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Opsoclonus-myoclonus-ataxia syndrome (OMAS) is rare in adults. Here, we report a rare case of OMAS in an elderly patient, accompanied by video documentation and a comprehensive literature review, which may offer valuable insights into the clinical features, diagnosis, and management of this condition. An 81-year-old female was admitted with limb tremors lasting for 1 day. During the hospitalization, she developed opsoclonus, myoclonus, ataxia, behavioral changes, and sleep disturbances. Laboratory and imaging findings were unremarkable, with no tumor detected during follow-up, supporting a diagnosis of idiopathic OMAS. Immunotherapy consisted of steroids, while symptomatic treatment included clonazepam and gabapentin. The patient showed marked symptomatic improvement after immunotherapy. At two-year follow-up, there was no evidence of recurrence or malignancy. In elderly patients, OMAS is extremely rare and often diagnosed and treated late. Comprehensive screening for malignancies and infectious triggers is critical. Early recognition and prompt immunotherapy improve outcomes.

papers.title: Cardiovascular Health Promotion for US Veterans: Current State, Gaps, and Strategies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
papers.abstract: US veterans represent a large and diverse population with distinctive demographic characteristics, comorbidity profiles, and social determinants of health shaped by military service. These factors contribute to a high burden of cardiovascular risk and low attainment of ideal cardiovascular health. At the same time, the Department of Veterans Affairs, which operates the nation's largest integrated healthcare system, provides a unique infrastructure for delivering population-level cardiovascular disease prevention for veterans. Understanding its successes and ongoing challenges can inform broader strategies across all health systems for promoting health among veterans. This scientific statement applies the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 framework, expanded to include mental health and substance use, to evaluate veteran cardiovascular health. For each domain, we review guideline recommendations, barriers to achieving optimal health, and major Veterans Affairs programs such as Patient Aligned Care Teams, the MOVE! Weight Management Program for Veterans, Whole Health, telehealth-based interventions, and integrated mental health and substance use disorder services. Across domains, veterans receiving Veterans Affairs care often achieve outcomes that are equal to or better than those of their non-Veterans Affairs counterparts, reflecting the strengths of the system in coordinated, team-based care and research-driven implementation. Despite substantial progress, opportunities remain to improve veteran lifestyle behaviors, metabolic health, lipid and blood pressure control, engagement in mental health and substance use care, and detection and management of sleep disorders. Addressing these challenges at the Veterans Affairs will require continuing to expand care access, enhancing digital data integration, tailoring interventions to high-risk subgroups, and strengthening implementation strategies to improve uptake and engagement across Veterans Affairs services.

papers.title: Aviation Medicine and Cardiovascular Assessment of Aircrew: A European Society of Cardiology-Aligned Review of Integrating International Civil Aviation Organization, European Union Aviation Safety Agency, Federal Aviation Administration, and Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation Aeromedical Standards.
papers.abstract: Aeromedical certification is based on a safety-first principle: a pilot or other aircrew member must not have a medical disorder that creates an unacceptable risk of sudden or subtle incapacitation during flight. Cardiovascular disease remains one of the most important determinants of flight fitness, as it may impair consciousness, judgment, rhythm stability, exercise capacity, and hemodynamic reserve. Modern aeromedical decision-making therefore requires the integration of aviation law, operational risk, contemporary cardiology guidelines, advanced imaging, biomarkers, and long-term surveillance. The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Annex 1 provides the global licensing framework; the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) Part-MED, together with its Acceptable Means of Compliance and Guidance Material, defines detailed operational standards in Europe; and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) employs a protocol- and special issuance-based system for many cardiovascular and metabolic disorders. This review summarizes the aeromedical assessment of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic and acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, cardiomy-opathies, arrhythmias and conduction disorders, pacemakers and implantable cardiac devices, valvular heart disease, aortic disease, congenital heart disease, venous throm-boembolism, cardiovascular pharmacotherapy, and major respiratory conditions rel-evant to flight certification. The manuscript is aligned with current European Society of Cardiology cardiovascular guidance and with the operational aeromedical principles applied by ICAO, EASA, FAA, and the Turkish Directorate General of Civil Aviation. In general, preserved ventricular function, absence of significant symptoms, low thrombo-embolic and arrhythmic risk, stable treatment, and adequate exercise capacity support certification or restricted certification. In contrast, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable diabetes, significant residual myocardial ischemia, reduced ejection fraction, malignant ventricular arrhythmias, implantable defibrillator therapy, severe valvular disease, significant aortic pathology, major congenital hemodynamic lesions, or poorly controlled sleep apnea usually preclude certification. Final decisions remain individualized and depend on license class, operational role, treatment burden, surveillance data, and the judgment of the aeromedical authority.

papers.title: Social media-related dietary behaviors and integrated behavioral model constructs among university students: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Social media exposes young adults to nutrition information, food marketing, peer norms, and health-related content. However, evidence on social media-related dietary behaviors and their links to Integrated Behavioral Model (IBM) constructs among Saudi university students is limited. This study examined these behaviors, IBM constructs, and factors associated with the Dietary Habits score among King Khalid University (KKU) students. A cross-sectional study included 385 KKU undergraduates, recruited through convenience sampling between February and April 2026. Participants completed the Arabic IBM-based Social Media and Dietary Habits Questionnaire. Analyses included descriptive statistics, Spearman's correlation, independent-samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc tests, and multiple linear regression. Regression coefficient p-values were adjusted using the Holm-Bonferroni procedure across the 32 coefficient tests. The mean dietary habits score was 12.06 ± 4.17. All IBM constructs were positively correlated with dietary habits (p < 0.001). Exploratory comparisons showed that Dietary Habits scores differed by gender, marital status, BMI, chronic illness, physical activity, smoking, sleep duration, healthy diet, and social media use. The regression model explained 57.6% of the variance in dietary scores (adjusted R² = 0.537). IBM constructs were positively interrelated and associated with social media-related dietary behaviors. Positive attitudes, physical activity, and moderate daily social media use were associated with higher Dietary Habits scores. These findings suggest that behavioral beliefs and lifestyle context may be relevant in the design of digital nutrition programs for university students.

papers.title: Can COVID-19 Cause Acute Psychosis in Pediatric Patients? A Case Report.
papers.abstract: To demonstrate that COVID-19-associated acute psychosis, though rare, can happen in the pediatric patient population. Patients with new-onset psychosis should be tested for COVID-19 infection, and other organic causes of psychosis should also be considered (e.g., delirium, medication-induced psychosis, and catatonia). Patient X, a 14-year-old female with no known past psychiatric history, presented to the local emergency room following odd behavior for 3 days and having tested positive for COVID-19 2 weeks prior. The patient's mother reported odd behaviors, including the patient claiming her fish was calling her name and her name was being repeated on TV. She had been moving slowly with occasional staring. The patient's mother reported episodes in which the patient was repeating phrases over and over and where she would require redirection to a task. When the patient planned to have a bath, her mother noted that she was naked in her room while looking for something and then needed redirection to go take a bath. She did not have any episodes of agitation. A thorough psychiatric evaluation indicated she was experiencing visual hallucinations. Her vitals were within normal ranges, except for a mildly elevated heart rate. The patient was admitted for further testing, assessment, and management. She was started on chlorpromazine 10 mg daily as needed for psychosis. A complete blood count with differential (CBC), complete metabolic panel (CMP), and thyroid function results were all within the normal range. Urine drug screening was negative. EKG, CSF analysis, chest X-ray, and brain MRI showed no significant abnormalities. Mild background slowing was noted on EEG, with no interictal/epileptiform discharges or any delta brushes. Therefore, a tentative diagnosis of COVID-19-associated psychosis was made. Treated with chlorpromazine 10 mg daily, the patient gradually improved with no hallucinations or bizarre behavior. She was discharged after 5 days and was not prescribed any medication at discharge. Nine days after discharge, the patient was seen by a pediatric neurologist. She did not report any hallucinations or delusions, but her mother reported that the patient moved slowly and had difficulty identifying common objects. An autoimmune panel, physical exam, and repeat EEG were all unremarkable. The neurologist concluded that her psychosis was most likely post-viral sequelae. The patient continued to improve and returned to school over the span of 2 months. Acute psychosis after COVID-19 infection is a new and emerging diagnosis with no consensus on management strategies for pediatric or adult patient populations. This case highlights the need for clinicians to be vigilant of subtle, fluid psychotic symptoms, in addition to patients' general mental well-being. We do not have research regarding the long-term consequences of acute psychosis episodes. Further studies are needed to investigate the neuropsychiatric etiology of post-COVID-19 psychosis and the optimum treatment for this group of patients. No Funding.
